  <name>Task 1: Characterize the dimension and coordinate math</name>
  <files>src/app/services/scaling.service.spec.ts</files>
  <read_first>
    - `src/app/services/scaling.service.ts` — the file under test, all 142 lines. Note `basePixelsPerUnit` is a `private readonly` set to 10, `calculateImageDimensions` takes `(sizeInches, scale, originalDimensions?)` with `originalDimensions` optional, and the measurement-line branch only fires when both `sizeInches.measurementLine` and `originalDimensions` are present AND the computed ruler length is strictly greater than zero.
    - `src/app/utils/coordinate-transform.spec.ts` — the pattern analog named in 05-PATTERNS.md (exact match: pure-math spec with hand-built stand-ins and no DI machinery). Copy its `describe`-per-function structure and its habit of naming the ratio being asserted in the spec title.
    - `.claude/skills/scaling-system/SKILL.md` — the invariants this spec must assert rather than contradict: scaling is uniform and center-based, there is no anchor-point scaling, transform-origin is used for rotation only, and Canvas and DOM renderers use identical math.
    - `src/app/models/image-model.interface.ts` — the `MeasurementLine` shape (`start`/`end` points) that `calculateMeasurementLineLength` consumes.
  </read_first>
  <action>
Create `src/app/services/scaling.service.spec.ts`. Unlike the `coordinate-transform` analog (free functions, no DI), `ScalingService` is `@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })`, so wrap it in a minimal `TestBed.configureTestingModule({ providers: [ScalingService] })` and obtain the instance with `TestBed.inject(ScalingService)` in a `beforeEach`. The service has no constructor dependencies, so no other providers are required.

Cover, in one `describe` block per method:

`calculateImageDimensions` — assert the base formula `height = sizeInches.height * 10 * scale`, deriving the expected number arithmetically in the spec title so a future reader can see where it comes from. Cover: the `originalDimensions` present case where width follows the aspect ratio `originalDimensions.width / originalDimensions.height`; the `originalDimensions` omitted fallback where width equals height (square assumption); a scale other than 1 to prove the multiplication is applied to both axes uniformly (this is the uniform-scaling invariant made testable); and the measurement-line branch, where the user's stated height is interpreted as the length along the ruler rather than the full image height, so effective height becomes `originalDimensions.height * (sizeInches.height / rulerPixelLength)`. Add a case where the measurement line's start and end are identical, so ruler length is zero and the guard must leave effective height untouched at `sizeInches.height` rather than producing `Infinity` or `NaN`. Add a case where a measurement line is supplied but `originalDimensions` is omitted, proving the branch requires both.

`calculateMeasurementLineLength` — assert Euclidean distance on a 3-4-5 triangle so the expected value is exact rather than floating-point-approximate, plus a zero-length line and a line whose end coordinates are smaller than its start (negative deltas must still yield a positive length).

`transformAttachmentPoint` — assert that a point expressed in ORIGINAL image pixel coordinates is scaled by the independent per-axis ratios `scaledDimensions.width / originalDimensions.width` and `scaledDimensions.height / originalDimensions.height`. Include the origin `{x: 0, y: 0}` (must stay at the origin — this is what "no anchor-point scaling" means concretely for this function) and a point at the exact bottom-right corner (must land on the scaled dimensions exactly). Name in a spec title, or in a short comment, that the input coordinate space is the original image and never the scaled one — that is the attachment-system invariant this function embodies.

Do not modify `src/app/services/scaling.service.ts` in this plan. This is a characterization spec: it records what the code does today so 05-09 can adjudicate the disputed geometry rows against evidence. If a case looks wrong while writing it, assert the observed behavior and add a comment flagging the doubt for 05-09 rather than changing the production math here.
  </action>

<task type="auto">
  <name>Task 2: Characterize overlay scale composition and the scaleState$ stream</name>
  <files>src/app/services/scaling.service.spec.ts</files>
  <read_first>
    - `src/app/services/scaling.service.ts` — `calculateOverlayScale` (composes `sizeRatio * baseScale * individualScale`, where `baseScale` is `parentScale` when `scaleRelativeToParent` is true and 1 otherwise), `updateLeftScale` / `updateRightScale` (both route through the private `clampScale`, bounds 0.1 and 10), and the `scaleState$` pipeline (`combineLatest` → `map` → `distinctUntilChanged` comparing only `leftScale` and `rightScale`).
    - `src/app/services/scaling.service.spec.ts` — the file as written in Task 1, so the new blocks match its existing structure and `beforeEach`.
    - `.claude/skills/scaling-system/SKILL.md` — for the meaning of `scaleRelativeToParent` and the relationship between an overlay's own scale and its parent's.
    - `src/app/components/image-display/image-display.component.spec.ts` — read the currently-failing `Overlay Positioning should handle scaleRelativeToParent correctly` spec. That failure is one of 05-09's rows; this task's job is to pin what the service actually computes so 05-09 can tell whether the component or the spec is at fault.
  </read_first>
  <action>
Extend `src/app/services/scaling.service.spec.ts` with two more `describe` blocks.

`calculateOverlayScale` — assert the composition for both settings of `scaleRelativeToParent`. With it true, the parent's scale participates: the result is `(overlayHeight / baseModelHeight) * parentScale * individualScale`. With it false, the parent's scale is excluded entirely and `baseScale` is 1, so the result is `(overlayHeight / baseModelHeight) * individualScale` — assert that changing `parentScale` while the flag is false leaves the result unchanged, which is the sharpest way to pin the branch. Include a case where overlay and base heights are equal (size ratio exactly 1) and a case where the overlay is smaller than the base, using numbers that divide cleanly so the expectations are exact rather than approximate.

`updateLeftScale` / `updateRightScale` / `scaleState$` — subscribe to `scaleState$` and assert:
- The initial emission has `leftScale` 1, `rightScale` 1, `relativeScale` 1, and `pixelsPerUnit` 10.
- After `updateLeftScale(2)`, the emission carries `leftScale` 2 and `relativeScale` 2 (`leftScale / rightScale`).
- After `updateRightScale(4)` on top of that, `relativeScale` is 0.5.
- Clamping at both bounds: a value below 0.1 emits 0.1, a value above 10 emits 10. Assert on the emitted state rather than on any private field.
- The `distinctUntilChanged` behavior: pushing the same left scale twice produces one emission, not two. Count emissions with a collector array rather than a spy on the observable, and note in a comment that the comparator only inspects `leftScale`/`rightScale` — `relativeScale` and `pixelsPerUnit` are derived, so they cannot independently trigger an emission.

Unsubscribe every subscription this block creates before the spec ends. `scaleState$` is backed by long-lived `BehaviorSubject`s on a root-provided service, so a leaked subscription persists across specs in the same Karma run and can make a later spec see emissions it did not cause.

Do not use `fakeAsync`/`tick` here — `combineLatest` over `BehaviorSubject`s emits synchronously on subscribe, so a plain collector array is sufficient and avoids importing zone-timing complexity into a pure-math spec.

Still do not modify `src/app/services/scaling.service.ts`.
  </action>
  <verify>

  </verify>
  <acceptance_criteria>

    - The spec contains a case asserting that with `scaleRelativeToParent` false, two different `parentScale` values produce the identical result.
    - The spec asserts an initial `scaleState$` emission with `pixelsPerUnit` equal to 10 and `relativeScale` equal to 1.
    - The spec asserts `relativeScale` equals 0.5 for left 2 / right 4.
    - The spec asserts clamping at both 0.1 and 10 by reading the emitted `ScaleState`, not a private field.
    - The spec asserts that a repeated identical scale update produces exactly one emission.
    - Every `subscribe` call in the new blocks has a matching `unsubscribe` before its spec ends.
    - `CHROME_BIN=/home/user/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium-1223/chrome-linux64/chrome pnpm exec ng test --no-watch --browsers=ChromeHeadless --include='**/scaling.service.spec.ts'` exits 0 with zero failures.
    - The full suite's failing count is no higher than the count recorded in `05-TRIAGE.md` — this plan adds specs and must not introduce cross-spec leakage.
    - `git diff --exit-code src/app/services/scaling.service.ts` succeeds.
  </acceptance_criteria>
  <done>Overlay scale composition and the `scaleState$` stream, including clamping and distinct-until-changed behavior, are characterized with no leaked subscriptions, and the targeted run is green.</done>
